Information since March points to solid real activity and a strong labor market, while inflation is running below 2 percent. The FOMC kept the funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent and maintained patient guidance, consistent with expectations management and a floor-system technical tweak to IOER.

Incorporating SLOOS: The April 2019 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates banks tightened standards on C&I and construction/land development loans and tightened other lending terms, while reporting weaker demand for HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans; auto loans and subprime residential mortgage demand were unchanged. These survey results point to a modestly more restrictive credit environment and softer loan demand, implying downside risks to business investment and some consumer credit categories despite strong labor data.

Together with the Financial Stability Report’s note of somewhat elevated valuations and high business debt vulnerabilities, the tone shifts from cautiously optimistic to more balanced with mild downside risks. Accordingly, the sentiment is marked down from the initial assessment.

sentiment score = 0.10
